items.title: 52220_Woody Herman oral history interview
items.q: in '44, I hired Hyams, Marjorie Hines, a very good vibra-harpist.

ctx.x: You were one of the first -- if not most of it -- people who had started to use female instrumentalists. You had Billie Rogers on trumpet.

Yeah, she was first with the band. That would be about '41, I think. And then later, in '44, I hired Hyams, Marjorie Hines, a very good vibra-harpist. As a matter of fact, she was there and then she was followed by Red Norvo, so she wound up in very good class. And when she left the band, she went with George Shearing's first sextet.
What was your feeling about incorporating the vibes and other instruments? You've had different instruments, because you had the guitar --
